_readme: Spec-parameter coverage matrix - the honest definition of conformance:
every request parameter the pinned SDKs enumerate has a deliberate,
a param in the SDK but not here FAILS the gate (new spec params must
get a disposition); a param here but not in the SDK is stale and FAILS.
implemented - real behavior, covered by the functional gates
partial     - accepted for a value subset, honest 400 otherwise
advisory    - accepted with spec semantics (telemetry/routing hints
with no server-side effect to have)
rejected    - honest 400 (explicit check or unknown-field rejection)
The gate probes every rejected/partial param (expects 400) and every
`_pinned` IS the pin, and the gate asserts the installed SDKs match it
before believing a single result. This is not hypothetical: the `python`
tests/sdk_conformance.rs invokes once sat months behind the pinned SDKs,
so the whole suite had been passing against a stale spec revision the
entire time. A stale SDK now fails the gate by name.
Bump: pip install -U openai==X anthropic==Y, edit `_pinned`, re-run.
_audio_readme: `/v1/audio/transcriptions` is multipart/form-data, not JSON, and it needs
a LOADED ASR model to answer anything - no other section does. So it
splits in two: the matrix audit above (SDK params vs dispositions) is
static and runs on every invocation, including boxes with no whisper
checkpoint, because that is the half that catches a new spec param. The
probes and the functional cases need a server and run under --audio-only
(sdk_conformance.rs::spec_gate_whisper starts one).
`timestamp_granularities` is implemented (closed it) but WHICH
values a given runner answers is a per-checkpoint fact, published on
/v1/models: whisper answers both, granite-speech-plus answers `word`
only, everything else neither. The functional half reads that list and
derives its expectations from it, so it runs against any lane and a
wrong advertisement fails on the assertions it selected.
`model` is advisory for the reason it is everywhere here: a runner serves
exactly one model, so the field names a deployment rather than selecting.
`stream` is implemented on all three lanes and refuses only
srt/vtt, where a partial document is not a partial answer. The gate holds
it to the invariant that matters: the deltas concatenate to done.text.
`prompt` is implemented on all three lanes but means a different thing on
each: whisper feeds it behind `<|startofprev|>` as a spelling/vocabulary
hint, the generative lanes carry it as instruction context.
The gate asserts only what a spec client can rely on - accepted, still a
transcript - plus the refusal of a control token smuggled in as text.
`languages` is PARTIAL, and the split is by VALUE rather than by lane: on
a whisper-family runner the codes become a SOFT PRIOR over the server's
own language detection - biasing, never filtering, so an out-of-set
language that dominates the posterior still wins. That is what separates
it from Azure's LID (which returns a candidate language even when none was
spoken) and from Deepgram's (which silently drops speech in a language you
did not name). A code outside the loaded checkpoint's own map is refused
by name, and so is `languages` on a generative ASR lane, which has no
detection to bias. The 400-probe uses an unknown code precisely because
that refuses on EVERY lane. `language` and `languages` together is a 400
too: they answer the same question two ways, and silently preferring one
would drop a field the caller set.
_nested_readme: The matrices above audit TOP-LEVEL request params only, which is where
conformance was quietly incomplete: the SDKs also define discriminated
unions for content parts, message roles, tool types and tool_choice, and
an unknown member of one of those used to reach the chat template. What
happened next depended on how that template was written - qwen's tests
`'text' in item` and skipped it, so the content VANISHED with a 200.
Measured: an unknown Responses content part, an unknown chat
role, a chat `custom` tool and every unserved Responses tool type were
all silently accepted. Each now has a disposition here and a probe.
Same vocabulary as above; `implemented` members are covered by the
functional gates, everything else is probed for an honest 400.
_extensions_readme: Extensions are ours, outside the SDK surface, and the gate holds them to
the same standard: each is exercised so a rename or a quiet removal fails.
`paddock_words` is the odd one - a RESPONSE field carrying per-word text
+ logprob + confidence, not a request param, because OpenAI's word object
carries no probability to put it on. It sits on each verbose_json SEGMENT
on the whisper lane, where the times live, and TOP-LEVEL on the generative
lanes, which have logprobs but no timestamp vocabulary and so no segments
to hang anything on. There it is opt-in via include=logprobs,
since carrying logprobs costs the decode its overlap fast path.
It retires into `words` when lands real word times.
`paddock_verbose` is the second: OpenAI's transcript.text.done carries
`text` and nothing else about the transcript, so a caller who streamed AND
asked for verbose_json would have to re-send the clip to get its segments.
It holds the exact object the non-streaming verbose_json returns.
`paddock_guards` is the third, and the only one that exists
because the spec cannot express the fact at all: an ASR decode can fail
without erroring - whisper writes a fluent sentence over a window of
silence, a model gets stuck repeating one token until the context bound
stops it. We now catch both (whisper.cpp's thresholds, minus its retry
ladder), and under the no-silent-failures principle a decode that was cut
or refused has to SAY so. Each entry is a SPAN - {start, end, reason,
text_dropped, note} plus whichever of no_speech_prob / avg_logprob /
entropy the lane could answer - and the key is ABSENT, never an empty
array, on the clips (every one in a clean battery) where nothing fired.
`text_dropped` separates the two remedies: a no_speech span has a positive
signal its audio held nothing, so the text goes; a cut decode keeps what
it said up to the cut. `text`, `srt` and `vtt` carry no notice - they have
nowhere to put one, the same way they have nowhere to put `duration`.
`paddock_guard_stats` is the fourth, the odd one out twice over: it is the
only extension asked for by a REQUEST field of the same name, and the only
one that exists for tuning rather than for reading. `paddock_guards` says
what fired; this says how close everything came, per window, whether or
not anything fired - entropy, avg_logprob, no_speech_prob,
compression_ratio, the stop reason, and the thresholds THIS build applies
so a sweep never has to hardcode our constants. It exists because task
#163 could otherwise only measure that nothing tripped, not whether the
margin was 0.79 nats or 8. It is also the honest end of a promise
`compression_ratio` has been making since  - "so the caller can
apply their own threshold" - which a caller cannot do on one number out
of four. Numbers a lane cannot answer are ABSENT, never zero: the
generative families have no no-speech head, and granite's timestamp mode
runs no entropy test to report.
`paddock_language` is the fifth, and like `paddock_guards` it
exists because the spec cannot express the fact at all. OpenAI's
`language` is one string with nowhere to say where it came from, how sure
the server was, what it nearly said instead, or whether the finished TEXT
is even in that language. The last one is load-bearing: a speech model
given the wrong language does not mislabel its output, it TRANSLATES, and
the result is fluent and grammatical with no ragged edge to notice. So the
object carries `source` (asked | detected | reported | unknown),
`probability` and `candidates` where a detector produced them, `hints`
(with `outranked` when the caller's candidate set overturned the model's
own answer - a soft prior is allowed to be strong, never invisible), and
`written`: the transcript's own language with `agrees`. A contradiction
ALSO raises a `language_mismatch` decode guard, so a plain-`json` caller
with no verbose body to look inside still learns their transcript may be a
translation rather than a transcription.
